message.content:
Yes—if you’re experiencing excessive or disruptive noise in Atlanta, you can bring it to the attention of your local city council. While the **City of Atlanta Police Department** is usually the first point of contact for immediate noise complaints, the city council has the authority to enact and enforce noise‑related ordinances and can address broader community concerns.

---

### How to File a Noise Complaint in Atlanta

| Step | Action | Details |
|------|--------|---------|
| 1 | Identify the source | Note the location, time, and duration of the noise. If possible, record audio or video evidence. |
| 2 | Contact the Police Department | Call **404‑656‑4000** (non‑emergency line) or visit the nearest precinct. For urgent situations, dial **911**. |
| 3 | Use the online portal | Go to the City of Atlanta’s official website and navigate to the “Noise Complaints” page. Fill out the form with all required details. |
| 4 | Follow up | You’ll receive a reference number. Keep it handy for any future correspondence. |

> **Tip:** If the noise issue persists after contacting the police, you can bring it to the next City Council meeting. Each council district holds regular meetings where residents can voice concerns.

---

### Relevant Ordinance

- **Title 10, Chapter 1, Section 10‑1‑2 – Noise Ordinance**  
  This ordinance sets permissible noise levels and outlines penalties for violations. It also provides guidelines for reporting and enforcement.

---

### Contact Information

| Agency | Phone | Website |
|--------|-------|---------|
| City of Atlanta Police Department | 404‑656‑4000 | [Atlanta Police](https://www.atlantaga.gov/Police) |
| City of Atlanta City Hall | 404‑656‑4000 | [City Hall](https://www.atlantaga.gov/CityHall) |
| City Council District Meetings | Check the city’s calendar | [Council Meetings](https://www.atlantaga.gov/CouncilMeetings) |

---

#### Quick Summary

- **Yes**, you can report noise complaints to your local council in Atlanta.  
- **First step:** Contact the City of Atlanta Police Department (online or by phone).  
- **If unresolved:** Bring the issue to your district’s City Council meeting.  

Feel free to let me know if you’d like more detailed guidance on filing the complaint or attending a council meeting!
